Capacity, demand, and utilization for each year

Source: R/visuals.R
plot_capacity_demand.Rd

One row per year. The default draws three columns. unit = "golfers" counts people. In the Dobson extract a round is one golfer, and capacity is the city's daylight estimate of golfers. unit = "slots" counts tee times. Slot capacity is that golfer estimate divided by players_per_slot. Slot demand is the fewest slots that could hold the golfers, rounding up. A group of 1, 2, or 3 golfers still uses a slot, and this file does not record group size, so slots actually used are not shown. panels chooses which columns to print.

Usage

plot_capacity_demand(
  data,
  calendar = NULL,
  unit = c("golfers", "slots"),
  players_per_slot = 4,
  panels = c("capacity", "utilization", "heatmap")
)

Arguments

data

Daily rows from dobson_operating_daily().

calendar

Optional operating_calendar().

unit

golfers or slots.

players_per_slot

Golfers a full slot can hold. Used only for slots. This is not a group size from the extract.

panels

Columns to print: capacity, utilization, and heatmap. The object still carries every column.

Value

A golfops_capacity_demand_plot. Printing it draws one row per year.

Details

The left column is capacity and demand, in ColorBrewer Dark2 gray and green, on a January–December axis and a shared scale. The middle column is utilization in ColorBrewer Dark2 purple, from 0 to 120 percent. A cross marks a day above 120 percent. The right column is that year's utilization heatmap. Its fill is ColorBrewer PRGn: green below the median played day, purple above it, and red above 100 percent. A missing date is black, and a zero-round day of unknown status is medium-dark gray. A cross marks a heatmap day above 120 percent. A zero-round day of unknown status and a missing date leave a gap in demand and in the utilization line.
